column1: # Random outcomes anchored on published host-clock re-seeds (`prng.md`
# Section 3), with no idle time between the re-seed and the draw it feeds.
# Run with a fixed DOS clock (the `# fixed-clock:` header below, which
# `paired_suite.py` applies): both sides then re-seed to the same state, so
# every outcome checked here must agree exactly, run after run. A difference
# in any of them is an engine draw defect, not a lottery.
# The seed is `seed-town-talk-reseeded` (Britain, the party south of the
# noble fighting bard) with two save bytes changed: the Falsehood hideout slot
# and torches are 2, 3 and 4, so the theft's first case applies.
#   * Journey Onward runs the preserving entry, whose Shadowlord install runs
#     the hideout blight (day-of-month seed, then a host-clock re-seed;
#     `town-mode.md` Section 3) and then the resident-entry sweep.
#   * `talk`: the bard is a stranger, so the opener re-seeds from the clock
#     (`conversation.md` Section 9 step 3). At 12:00:00.00 the seed is
#     `0x09EB` and the first draw is odd.
#   * `bye`: an empty line ends the conversation, and in the Falsehood
#     hideout the cleanup prints `Something was stolen!`, re-seeds, and
#     draws over keys, gems and torches until it lands on one the party
#     carries (`conversation.md` Section 10). At this seed that draw is the
#   * `p1`..`p3`: Z-stats, to read which of the three counters lost one.
